title: Relative rank-one centralizer of a root kernel torus
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. An $S$-group scheme is a group object in schemes over $S$ [def-pc-scheme], with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] over this base. Put $\mathbf G_{m,S}=\operatorname{Spec}A[t,t^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units and $\mathbf G_{a,S}=\operatorname{Spec}A[x]$ with addition. For a smooth group $H/S$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], write $\operatorname{Lie}(H)=\ker(H(A[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))\to H(A))$, with addition from multiplication and scalar action from $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$. Let $G/S$ be smooth affine of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] with every geometric fibre connected reductive: it has no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup, where unipotent means unipotent geometric matrices in a faithful representation. Let $T=\mathbf G_{m,S}^r\hookrightarrow G$ be a closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion] which is a maximal torus on every geometric fibre, with $r\geq0$, $M=\mathbf Z^r$, characters $\chi_m(z)=z^m$, and conjugation weight modules $\mathfrak g_m\subseteq\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ defined by the coaction equation $\rho(v)=v\otimes z^m$. Suppose $\alpha\in M\setminus\{0\}$ and $\mathfrak g_\alpha$ is locally free of rank one. Write $\alpha=d\alpha_0$ with $d>0$ and $\alpha_0$ primitive, and put $T_\alpha=\ker\chi_{\alpha_0}$, a split torus of rank $r-1$ (the trivial group if $r=1$). The centralizer functor
$$H(B)=\{g\in G(B):g_Cu=ug_C\text{ for every }B\text{-algebra }C\text{ and }u\in T_\alpha(C)\}$$
is represented by a smooth affine finitely presented closed subgroup $H\subseteq G$ with connected reductive geometric fibres and with $T_\alpha$ central in $H$. One has
$$\operatorname{Lie}(H)=\operatorname{Lie}(T)\oplus\mathfrak g_\alpha\oplus\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}\subseteq\mathfrak g,$$
and $\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}$ is locally free of rank one. Each geometric fibre of $(H,T)$ has precisely the nonzero roots $\{\alpha,-\alpha\}$. These centralizer, Lie inclusion and weight-module identifications commute with arbitrary and successive ring base changes. Here connectedness is [def-weil-connected-scheme], and a torus over an algebraically closed field is a product of multiplicative groups. No global trivialization of either root line is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-torus-centralizer-normalizer] with the rank-zero torus in $G$: its centralizer is $G$ itself. This supplies the finite locally free tangent module $\mathfrak g$ and its natural arbitrary-base-change comparisons. Work on affine open neighbourhoods where this module is finite free, hence finite projective. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-torus-bundle-weights] there to the conjugation coaction. Its coefficient projections are uniquely determined by $\rho(v)=\sum_m v_m\otimes z^m$, so agree on intersections. Thus they give $\mathfrak g=\bigoplus_m\mathfrak g_m$ globally, with finite projective summands on each such neighbourhood and arbitrary-base-change comparisons. A finite subcover exists since the base is affine; the union of its finite weight supports is finite. The tangent operations are the stipulated ones: writing a tangent point as $e+\epsilon D$, the unit identities for group multiplication make the product have coefficient $D+E$, while $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$ multiplies $D$ by $a$.

proof.text: Put $L=\mathbf Z\alpha_0=M\cap\mathbf Q\alpha$. Primitive means that the coordinates of $\alpha_0$ have greatest common divisor one. Integer elementary row operations, using Euclidean division on successive coordinate pairs, carry $\alpha_0$ to the first standard basis vector. They give Laurent-monomial changes of coordinates identifying $M/L$ with $\mathbf Z^{r-1}$ and $T_\alpha$ with $\mathbf G_m^{r-1}$. Equivalently its coordinate map is $A[M]\twoheadrightarrow A[M/L]$, $z^m\mapsto z^{\bar m}$; its kernel is generated by $z^{\alpha_0}-1$. It is a closed subgroup of $T$ and hence of $G$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-torus-centralizer-normalizer] to this split torus. Its functor is exactly the displayed universal commuting functor in the item, so it gives $H$ smooth affine finitely presented and closed in $G$, with $\operatorname{Lie}(H)=\mathfrak g^{T_\alpha}$, and gives arbitrary base change for these identifications. Here $\alpha\ne0$ implies $r\geq1$.

proof.text: Fix any geometric point $\bar s$ of $S$. Step 1 identifies $\mathfrak g_m\otimes_A\kappa(\bar s)$ with the full character-weight space in $\operatorname{Lie}(G_{\bar s})$. The assumed line $\mathfrak g_\alpha$ therefore makes $\alpha$ a root there. Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections] to the connected reductive group $G_{\bar s}$ and its split maximal torus $T_{\bar s}$. Its statement gives the zero-weight space $\operatorname{Lie}(T_{\bar s})$, dimension one for both opposite root spaces, and $\Phi_{\bar s}\cap\mathbf Q\alpha=\{\alpha,-\alpha\}$. Moreover the centralizer of the largest subtorus killed by $\alpha$ is connected reductive of semisimple rank one. That subtorus is $(T_\alpha)_{\bar s}$: by step 2 it is a torus, contained in $\ker\alpha$ since $\chi_\alpha=\chi_{\alpha_0}^d$; conversely, on a subtorus $U\cong\mathbf G_m^k$ of $\ker\alpha$ the restriction of $\chi_{\alpha_0}$ is a character with trivial $d$-th power, and characters of $\mathbf G_m^k$ are the grouplike elements, i.e. the monomials, of $\kappa(\bar s)[\mathbf Z^k]$, with $\mathbf Z^k$ torsion free, so $U\subseteq\ker\chi_{\alpha_0}$. That centralizer is $H_{\bar s}$ by the base-change clause of [lem-sfb-relative-torus-centralizer-normalizer]. Thus all geometric fibres of $H$ are connected reductive. Since $T\subseteq H$ and $T_{\bar s}$ is maximal in $G_{\bar s}$, it is also maximal in $H_{\bar s}$.

source.place: Propositions 21.1-21.2, printed pp.424-425, and Theorem 21.11(a)-(b), printed pp.428-429.

proof.text: On each affine neighbourhood used in step 1, every $\mathfrak g_m$ is finite projective by [lem-sfb-relative-torus-bundle-weights]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-prime-local-free], near any prime it is a finite free module. Its free rank is its dimension after passing to an algebraic closure of that prime's residue field. Step 3 therefore shows that $\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}$ is locally free of rank one, and that $\mathfrak g_m=0$ for $m\in L\setminus\{0,\alpha,-\alpha\}$. For the latter conclusion the free rank is zero on each such neighbourhood, so all prime localizations vanish. Explicitly, if a vector $v$ were nonzero, its proper annihilator would be contained in a maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$; $v/1=0$ at $\mathfrak p$ would give $a\notin\mathfrak p$ with $av=0$, a contradiction. Thus vanishing is over $A$, even when $A$ is nonreduced; it is not an inference that a matrix vanishing on reduced fibres vanishes over $A$.

source.place: Tag 00NX, lemma-finite-projective, finite projective implies finite locally free; elementary local-basis arguments below.

proof.text: Conjugation by $T$ on itself is trivial, so the tangent inclusion induces $j:A^r=\operatorname{Lie}(T)\to\mathfrak g_0$. The identification $\operatorname{Lie}(T)=A^r$ sends $(a_i)$ to the tuple of units $(1+\epsilon a_i)$, and is valid over every $A$-algebra. By [lem-sfb-relative-torus-bundle-weights] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-prime-local-free], on the affine neighbourhoods of step 1 the target is finite free locally at each prime. Step 3 and the tangent and weight comparisons of [lem-sfb-relative-torus-centralizer-normalizer] show that every geometric fibre of $j$ is the isomorphism onto the zero-weight space in [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections]. Choose a free neighbourhood at a prime $\mathfrak p$; the target rank is $r$ by that fibre isomorphism. The matrix of $j$ there is square and its determinant is outside $\mathfrak p$, since it becomes invertible over the algebraic closure of the residue field. Inverting that determinant makes $j$ invertible, with inverse its adjugate divided by its determinant. These neighbourhoods cover $S$, so $j$ is an isomorphism. It identifies the actual submodules $\operatorname{Lie}(T)=\mathfrak g_0$ of $\mathfrak g$.

proof.text: Apply the restriction-invariants clause of [lem-sfb-relative-torus-bundle-weights] to $L\subset M$ and the free quotient $M/L$. Together with [lem-sfb-relative-torus-centralizer-normalizer] this gives $\operatorname{Lie}(H)=\bigoplus_{m\in L}\mathfrak g_m$. Steps 4-5 turn this into precisely $\operatorname{Lie}(T)\oplus\mathfrak g_\alpha\oplus\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}$ inside $\mathfrak g$. After any geometric base change it has exactly the two nonzero characters $\alpha,-\alpha$. Finally $T_\alpha$ lies in $H$ because it commutes with itself, and every point of $H$ commutes universally with $T_\alpha$ by the defining functor. This proves that $T_\alpha$ is central in $H$.

proof.text: For $A\to B$, the Laurent quotient $B[M]\to B[M/L]$ is obtained from that of step 2 by tensoring, so $(T_\alpha)_B$ is the same root-kernel torus for $G_B$. The centralizer comparison in [lem-sfb-relative-torus-centralizer-normalizer] identifies $H_B$ with its centralizer as subfunctors of $G_B$: on every $B$-algebra both demand precisely the same universal commutation. Thus this identification and its inclusion in $G_B$ commute with a further extension $B\to B'$, since all the maps are the identity on the corresponding $G$-points. The tangent comparisons from the same node, and the weight and invariant comparisons in [lem-sfb-relative-torus-bundle-weights], identify $B\otimes_A\mathfrak g_m$ with $(\operatorname{Lie}(G_B))_m$ and $B\otimes_A\operatorname{Lie}(H)$ with $\operatorname{Lie}(H_B)$, with their inclusions. For successive extensions $A\to B\xrightarrow{h}B'$, write a tangent vector as a derivation $D$ at the identity. The comparison on $b\otimes D$ has coefficient $bD(c)$ on a coordinate $c$ of $G$. Both successive and direct comparisons on $b'\otimes(b\otimes D)$ have coefficient $b'h(b)D(c)$; therefore they agree, since pure tensors generate. Restricting this formula to each homogeneous summand proves the asserted successive compatibility for the root lines, zero weight and invariant module. All decomposition maps are inclusions and sums of these summands, so they agree too. No flatness assumption on $B$, basis of a root line, or restriction on residue characteristic has entered. If $A=0$ all schemes and modules here are empty or zero, so the assertions hold; if $r=0$ there is no allowed $\alpha$.
